raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Allow native SGLang Diffusion pipelines to use a single-file Tiny AutoEncoder
checkpoint for approximate image and video reconstruction. This provides an
optional lightweight final decoder while preserving the original VAE encoder
and latent metadata for conditioning inputs.

The existing FLUX.2 Tiny AutoEncoder component override remains available.

## Modifications

- Add `--tiny-vae-model` and `--tiny-vae-path`, with matching Python pipeline
  configuration fields. Reject incomplete option pairs and the Diffusers backend.
- Add MIT-licensed TAESD and TAEHV network implementations covering SD/SDXL,
  SD3, FLUX.1, FLUX.2, Qwen Image 2.1, HunyuanVideo, Wan2.1/2.2,
  HunyuanVideo 1.5, MiniMax-H3, and LTX-2 architectures. Accept ComfyUI video
  checkpoint names as aliases. Architecture support does not add generation
  pipelines for models that SGLang does not already support.
- Load full or decoder-only tensor state dictionaries from safetensors or
  PyTorch checkpoints through the existing weight resolver. Validate decoder
  keys strictly and reuse the configured VAE decode precision.
- Wrap the original visual VAE to preserve pipeline latent and pixel contracts,
  including FLUX.2 patchification, H3 pixel normalization, and LTX latent
  denormalization. Original conditioning encodes, text encoders, and audio VAEs
  retain their existing paths.
- Add focused tests and CLI documentation with checkpoint/model mappings.

Example with locally downloaded FLUX.1 Tiny AutoEncoder decoder weights:

```bash
sglang generate \
  --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev \
  --prompt "A lighthouse beside a calm ocean" \
  --tiny-vae-model taef1 \
  --tiny-vae-path /path/to/taef1_decoder.pth \
  --vae-decode-precision fp32 \
  --num-gpus 1 \
  --save-output
```

Limitations: TinyVAE changes reconstruction quality. Original VAE weights remain
loaded. TinyVAE spatial tiling, parallel decoding, layerwise VAE offload, and
incremental frame streaming are not implemented. LTX-2.3/2.5 require separately
trained weights and are rejected for `taeltx2`; TinyVAE cannot be combined with
the LTX diffusion decoder.

## Accuracy Tests

Remote CPU validation in the existing test environment:

- **88 tests passed; 11 subtests passed**, covering the new TinyVAE tests and
  existing VAE loading, decode precision, and decoding parallelism tests.
- Image architectures with 4/16/64/128 latent channels and video architectures
  with 16/24/32/48/128 channels matched the supplied ComfyUI encode/decode
  references. Video comparisons covered batch=2, temporal lengths, and memory
  reset between requests.
- A real MiniMax-H3 TinyVAE checkpoint matched the ComfyUI decoder bit for bit
  on CPU for batch=2 and latent lengths 1, 2, 7, and 37. The H3 pixel contract
  conversion remained finite.
- A decoding-stage test verifies that final pixels and the frame callback
  actually come from the TinyVAE decoder.

```bash
SGLANG_DIFFUSION_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE=cpu OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 \
python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_tiny_vae.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_vae_loader.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_vae_loader_decode_dtype.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_decoding_stage_parallelism.py
```

These results were obtained before migration to the latest upstream base; all
eight changed files were verified byte-identical after migration. No runtime
tests have been rerun on the new base. End-to-end GPU generation and
reconstruction quality across model families remain unverified.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No end-to-end latency or peak-memory benchmark has been run for this
implementation. No quantitative speedup or memory reduction is claimed.
Before marking this PR ready for merge, compare the original VAE and matching
TinyVAE with the same model, seed, prompt, resolution, duration, sampling steps,
precision, and device allocation, and attach the decode-stage timing, total
latency, peak memory, and representative output-quality results.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Selected Ruff lint rules, Ruff formatting, AST parsing, and Git whitespace checks passed; the complete pre-commit suite has not been run.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). CPU correctness results are included; end-to-end GPU and performance results are pending.
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Pending final contributor review.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Request review from the Diffusion Merge Oncalls through the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Obtain approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Ask an authorized contributor to trigger CI, for example with `/tag-and-rerun-ci`.
4. After green CI, completed validation, and required approvals, ask a maintainer to merge.

@@ -464,6 +464,84 @@ export SGLANG_S3_ENDPOINT_URL=https://minio.example.com
 
 See [Environment Variables](/docs/sglang-diffusion/environment_variables) for the full set of storage options.
 
+## TinyVAE decoding
+
+You can use a Tiny AutoEncoder checkpoint for approximate final image or video
+decoding with the native SGLang Diffusion backend. Supply both
+`--tiny-vae-path` and `--tiny-vae-model`. The original VAE remains loaded for
+conditioning encodes and latent metadata; text encoders and audio VAEs keep their
+normal execution paths.
+
+Example for an existing Linux CUDA installation, one GPU, with locally downloaded
+FLUX.1 Tiny AutoEncoder decoder weights:
+
+```bash
+sglang generate \
+  --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev \
+  --prompt "A lighthouse beside a calm ocean" \
+  --tiny-vae-model taef1 \
+  --tiny-vae-path /path/to/taef1_decoder.pth \
+  --vae-decode-precision fp32 \
+  --num-gpus 1 \
+  --save-output
+```
+
+The same two options work with `sglang serve`. Python pipeline configurations
+accept `tiny_vae_model` and `tiny_vae_path` with the same meanings. Model downloads
+may require your normal Hugging Face access token and model license acceptance.
+
+Choose the architecture explicitly; several different VAEs have the same latent
+channel count. The checkpoint must match the model's latent space.
+
+| Architecture | Target latent space | Latent channels |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `taesd` | Stable Diffusion 1.x/2.x | 4 |
+| `taesdxl` | SDXL | 4 |
+| `taesd3` | Stable Diffusion 3/3.5 | 16 |
+| `taef1` | FLUX.1 | 16 |
+| `taef2` | FLUX.2 (patchified latents) | 128 |
+| `taeqi2_1` | Qwen Image 2.1 (RGBA) | 64 |
+| `taehv` | HunyuanVideo | 16 |
+| `taew2_1` | Wan2.1, Wan2.2 14B, Qwen Image with Wan VAE | 16 |
+| `taew2_2` | Wan2.2 5B | 48 |
+| `taehv1_5` | HunyuanVideo 1.5 | 32 |
+| `taeh3` | MiniMax-H3 | 24 |
+| `taeltx2` | LTX-2 | 128 |
+
+The ComfyUI checkpoint names `lighttaew2_1`, `lighttaew2_2`,
+`lighttaehy1_5`, and `taeltx_2` are accepted as aliases for the corresponding
+video architectures above. Architecture compatibility does not establish
+reconstruction quality for an independently trained checkpoint.
+
+Architecture availability does not add a generation pipeline for a model that
+SGLang does not already support. For example, SD1/SDXL and HunyuanVideo 1.5 weights
+are supported by the TinyVAE network implementation, but require a matching
+native generation pipeline. LTX-2.3/2.5 use different trained VAEs; `taeltx2`
+weights are rejected for those decoder variants. TinyVAE cannot be combined with
+the LTX diffusion decoder.
+
+Use checkpoints from [TAESD](https://github.com/madebyollin/taesd) or
+[TAEHV](https://github.com/madebyollin/taehv), or compatible checkpoints with the
+same architecture. Full and decoder-only tensor state dictionaries are supported
+in `.safetensors`, `.pth`, `.pt`, or `.bin` format. Decoder keys may be unprefixed,
+`decoder.*`, or `taesd_decoder.*`. Encoder weights and ComfyUI `vae_scale` /
+`vae_shift` metadata are ignored: SGLang supplies the original pipeline's latent
+normalization. Missing or unexpected decoder weights fail loading. A Hugging Face
+single-file weight reference can also be passed through SGLang's weight resolver.
+
+TinyVAE trades reconstruction fidelity for cheaper decoding. It does not preserve
+the original VAE's output. The original VAE still costs loading time and weight
+memory. Component residency and `--vae-cpu-offload` apply to the original VAE and
+TinyVAE together. TinyVAE uses sequential temporal processing with fresh memory
+for each request; original VAE spatial tiling and parallel decode settings do not
+tile or distribute the TinyVAE decoder. Frame callbacks receive the completed clip.
+Layerwise VAE offload is unsupported; use resident or component offload placement.
+Request-scoped decode precision changes are unsupported with TinyVAE. If you set
+`--vae-decode-precision-high`, it must resolve to the same precision as the default
+decode, including any component precision override; otherwise loading fails.
+Start with `--vae-decode-precision fp32` when checking a new checkpoint, then
+validate reduced precision and output quality on your target hardware.
+
 ## Component Path Overrides
 
 Override individual pipeline components such as `vae`, `transformer`, or `text_encoder` with `--<component>-path`.

+"""Tiny AutoEncoder networks adapted from madebyollin/taesd and taehv.
+
+Image tensors use BCHW and video tensors use BCTHW. Encoder inputs and decoder
+outputs use unit-range pixels; latent inputs follow each trained checkpoint's
+diffusion-normalized latent space. Video memories belong to a single call.
+"""
+
+from collections import deque
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+from torch.nn import functional as F
+
+
+def conv(n_in, n_out, **kwargs):
+    return nn.Conv2d(n_in, n_out, 3, padding=1, **kwargs)
+
+
+class Clamp(nn.Module):
+    def forward(self, x):
+        return torch.tanh(x / 3) * 3
+
+
+class Block(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, n_in, n_out, use_midblock_gn=False):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.conv = nn.Sequential(
+            conv(n_in, n_out),
+            nn.ReLU(),
+            conv(n_out, n_out),
+            nn.ReLU(),
+            conv(n_out, n_out),
+        )
+        self.skip = (
+            nn.Conv2d(n_in, n_out, 1, bias=False) if n_in != n_out else nn.Identity()
+        )
+        self.fuse = nn.ReLU()
+        self.pool = None
+        if use_midblock_gn:
+            conv1x1, n_gn = (
+                lambda n_in, n_out: nn.Conv2d(n_in, n_out, 1, bias=False),
+                n_in * 4,
+            )
+            self.pool = nn.Sequential(
+                conv1x1(n_in, n_gn),
+                nn.GroupNorm(4, n_gn),
+                nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
+                conv1x1(n_gn, n_in),
+            )
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        if self.pool is not None:
+            x = x + self.pool(x)
+        return self.fuse(self.conv(x) + self.skip(x))
+
+
+def Encoder(latent_channels=4, use_midblock_gn=False, image_channels=3):
+    mb_kw = dict(use_midblock_gn=use_midblock_gn)
+    return nn.Sequential(
+        conv(image_channels, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        conv(64, 64, stride=2, bias=False),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        conv(64, 64, stride=2, bias=False),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        conv(64, 64, stride=2, bias=False),
+        Block(64, 64, **mb_kw),
+        Block(64, 64, **mb_kw),
+        Block(64, 64, **mb_kw),
+        conv(64, latent_channels),
+    )
+
+
+def Decoder(latent_channels=4, use_midblock_gn=False, image_channels=3):
+    mb_kw = dict(use_midblock_gn=use_midblock_gn)
+    return nn.Sequential(
+        Clamp(),
+        conv(latent_channels, 64),
+        nn.ReLU(),
+        Block(64, 64, **mb_kw),
+        Block(64, 64, **mb_kw),
+        Block(64, 64, **mb_kw),
+        nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2),
+        conv(64, 64, bias=False),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2),
+        conv(64, 64, bias=False),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2),
+        conv(64, 64, bias=False),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        conv(64, image_channels),
+    )
+
+
+def F16Encoder(latent_channels=64, image_channels=3):
+    """Encoder variant with 16x spatial downscaling, 2x2 input patchify, and wider low-res stages."""
+    return nn.Sequential(
+        nn.PixelUnshuffle(2),
+        conv(image_channels * 4, 64),
+        nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        conv(64, 64, stride=2, bias=False),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        conv(64, 128, stride=2, bias=False),
+        Block(128, 128),
+        Block(128, 128),
+        Block(128, 128),
+        conv(128, 256, stride=2, bias=False),
+        Block(256, 256),
+        Block(256, 256),
+        Block(256, 256),
+        conv(256, latent_channels),
+    )
+
+
+def F16Decoder(latent_channels=64, image_channels=3):
+    """Decoder variant with 16x spatial upscaling, wider low-res stages, and 2x2 output patchify."""
+    return nn.Sequential(
+        Clamp(),
+        conv(latent_channels, 256),
+        nn.ReLU(),
+        Block(256, 256),
+        Block(256, 256),
+        Block(256, 256),
+        nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2),
+        conv(256, 128, bias=False),
+        Block(128, 128),
+        Block(128, 128),
+        Block(128, 128),
+        nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2),
+        conv(128, 64, bias=False),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2),
+        conv(64, 64, bias=False),
+        Block(64, 64),
+        conv(64, image_channels * 4),
+        nn.PixelShuffle(2),
+    )
+
+
+class TinyImageAutoencoder(nn.Module):
+    """TAESD family operating on diffusion-normalized image latents."""
+
+    def __init__(self, latent_channels=4, load_encoder=True, load_decoder=True):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.latent_channels = latent_channels
+        self.image_channels = 4 if latent_channels == 64 else 3
+        channels = 32 if latent_channels == 128 else latent_channels
+        encoder = F16Encoder if latent_channels == 64 else Encoder
+        decoder = F16Decoder if latent_channels == 64 else Decoder
+        kwargs = {"image_channels": self.image_channels}
+        if latent_channels == 128:
+            kwargs["use_midblock_gn"] = True
+        self.encoder = encoder(channels, **kwargs) if load_encoder else None
+        self.decoder = decoder(channels, **kwargs) if load_decoder else None
+
+    def encode(self, pixels):
+        latents = self.encoder(pixels)
+        if self.latent_channels == 128:
+            b, c, h, w = latents.shape
+            latents = latents.reshape(b, c, h // 2, 2, w // 2, 2)
+            latents = latents.permute(0, 1, 3, 5, 2, 4).reshape(b, 128, h // 2, w // 2)
+        return latents
+
+    def decode(self, latents):
+        video = latents.ndim == 5
+        if video:
+            b, c, t, h, w = latents.shape
+            latents = latents.transpose(1, 2).reshape(b * t, c, h, w)
+        if self.latent_channels == 128:
+            b_images, _, h, w = latents.shape
+            latents = latents.reshape(b_images, 32, 2, 2, h, w)
+            latents = latents.permute(0, 1, 4, 2, 5, 3).reshape(
+                b_images, 32, h * 2, w * 2
+            )
+        pixels = self.decoder(latents)
+        if video:
+            pixels = pixels.reshape(b, t, *pixels.shape[1:]).transpose(1, 2)
+        return pixels
+
+
+class MemBlock(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, channels, leaky=False):
+        super().__init__()
+
+        def activation():
+            return nn.LeakyReLU(0.2, inplace=True) if leaky else nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
+
+        self.conv = nn.Sequential(
+            conv(channels * 2, channels),
+            activation(),
+            conv(channels, channels),
+            activation(),
+            conv(channels, channels),
+        )
+        self.act = activation()
+
+    def forward(self, x, past):
+        return self.act(self.conv(torch.cat((x, past), dim=1)) + x)
+
+
+class TemporalPool(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, channels, stride):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.stride = stride
+        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(channels * stride, channels, 1, bias=False)
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        _, c, h, w = x.shape
+        return self.conv(x.reshape(-1, self.stride * c, h, w))
+
+
+class TemporalGrow(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, channels, stride):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.stride = stride
+        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(channels, channels * stride, 1, bias=False)
+
+    def forward(self, x):
+        _, c, h, w = x.shape
+        return self.conv(x).reshape(-1, c, h, w)
+
+
+def _run_video_layers(layers, x, patch_size, decode):
+    batch = x.shape[0]
+    memory = [None] * len(layers)
+    queue = deque((frame, 0) for frame in x.unbind(1))
+    output = []
+    while queue:
+        frame, index = queue.popleft()
+        if index == 0 and not decode:
+            frame = F.pixel_unshuffle(frame, patch_size)
+        if index == len(layers):
+            output.append(F.pixel_shuffle(frame, patch_size) if decode else frame)
+            continue
+        layer = layers[index]
+        if isinstance(layer, MemBlock):
+            past = torch.zeros_like(frame) if memory[index] is None else memory[index]
+            result = layer(frame, past)
+            memory[index] = frame.detach().clone()
+            queue.appendleft((result, index + 1))
+        elif isinstance(layer, TemporalPool):
+            if memory[index] is None:
+                memory[index] = []
+            memory[index].append(frame)
+            if len(memory[index]) == layer.stride:
+                packed = torch.stack(memory[index], dim=1).flatten(0, 1)
+                queue.appendleft((layer(packed), index + 1))
+                memory[index] = []
+        elif isinstance(layer, TemporalGrow):
+            grown = layer(frame).reshape(batch, layer.stride, *frame.shape[1:])
+            for result in reversed(grown.unbind(1)):
+                queue.appendleft((result, index + 1))
+        else:
+            queue.appendleft((layer(frame), index + 1))
+    return torch.stack(output, dim=1)
+
+
+class TinyVideoAutoencoder(nn.Module):
+    """TAEHV family with request-local temporal memories."""
+
+    def __init__(self, latent_channels=16, load_encoder=True, load_decoder=True):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.latent_channels = latent_channels
+        self.patch_size = {24: 2, 32: 2, 48: 2, 128: 4}.get(latent_channels, 1)
+        self.temporal_ratio = 8 if latent_channels == 128 else 4
+        self.is_h3 = latent_channels == 24
+        leaky = latent_channels == 32
+
+        def activation():
+            return nn.LeakyReLU(0.2, inplace=True) if leaky else nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
+
+        encoder = [conv(3 * self.patch_size**2, 64), activation()]
+        for stride in (2, 2, 2) if latent_channels == 128 else (2, 2, 1):
+            encoder.extend(
+                [
+                    TemporalPool(64, stride),
+                    conv(64, 64, stride=2, bias=False),
+                    MemBlock(64, leaky),
+                    MemBlock(64, leaky),
+                    MemBlock(64, leaky),
+                ]
+            )
+        encoder.append(conv(64, latent_channels))
+        decoder = [Clamp(), conv(latent_channels, 256), activation()]
+        strides = (2, 2, 2) if latent_channels == 128 else (1, 2, 2)
+        for channels, next_channels, stride in zip(
+            (256, 128, 64), (128, 64, 64), strides
+        ):
+            decoder.extend(
+                [
+                    MemBlock(channels, leaky),
+                    MemBlock(channels, leaky),
+                    MemBlock(channels, leaky),
+                    nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2),
+                    TemporalGrow(channels, stride),
+                    conv(channels, next_channels, bias=False),
+                ]
+            )
+        decoder.extend([activation(), conv(64, 3 * self.patch_size**2)])
+        self.encoder = nn.Sequential(*encoder) if load_encoder else None
+        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(*decoder) if load_decoder else None
+
+    def encode(self, pixels):
+        x = pixels.transpose(1, 2)
+        b, time = x.shape[:2]
+        if self.is_h3:
+            x = torch.cat((x, x[:, -1:].expand(-1, -time % 17, -1, -1, -1)), dim=1)
+            x = F.pad(x.reshape(b, -1, 17, *x.shape[2:]), (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 0))
+            x = torch.cat(
+                [
+                    _run_video_layers(self.encoder, chunk, self.patch_size, False)
+                    for chunk in x.unbind(1)
+                ],
+                dim=1,
+            )
+            x = x[:, :1] if time == 1 else x[:, :-3]
+        else:
+            x = torch.cat(
+                (x, x[:, -1:].expand(-1, -time % self.temporal_ratio, -1, -1, -1)),
+                dim=1,
+            )
+            x = _run_video_layers(self.encoder, x, self.patch_size, False)
+        return x.transpose(1, 2)
+
+    def decode(self, latents):
+        if (
+            latents.ndim != 5
+            or latents.shape[1] != self.latent_channels
+            or latents.shape[2] < 1
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Tiny video latents must be [B,{self.latent_channels},T,H,W] with T >= 1"
+            )
+        x = _run_video_layers(
+            self.decoder, latents.transpose(1, 2), self.patch_size, True
+        )
+        trim = self.temporal_ratio - 1
+        if self.is_h3 and latents.shape[2] != 1:
+            x = F.pad(x, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, -x.shape[1] % 20))
+            x = x.unflatten(1, (-1, 20))[:, :, trim:].flatten(1, 2)
+            x = x[:, :-12]
+        else:
+            x = x[:, trim:]
+        return x.transpose(1, 2).clamp(0, 1)

+def validate_tiny_vae_config(config):
+    if not config.tiny_vae_path and not config.tiny_vae_model:
+        return
+    if bool(config.tiny_vae_path) != bool(config.tiny_vae_model):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "--tiny-vae-path and --tiny-vae-model must be supplied together"
+        )
+    model_name = TINY_VAE_ALIASES.get(config.tiny_vae_model, config.tiny_vae_model)
+    if model_name not in TINY_VAE_MODELS:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Unknown TinyVAE model {config.tiny_vae_model!r}; "
+            f"choose from {', '.join(TINY_VAE_MODELS)}"
+        )
+    if model_name == "taeltx2":
+        variant = getattr(config.vae_config.arch_config, "video_decoder_variant", None)
+        if variant != "ltx_2":
+            raise ValueError(
+                "taeltx2 weights target LTX-2; LTX-2.3/2.5 require separately trained weights"
+            )
+
+
+def load_tiny_autoencoder(path, model_name, dtype):
+    """Restore full checkpoints or decoder-only weights with strict decoder keys."""
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.loader.utils import initialize_model
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.weights.source import (
+        materialize_weight,
+        resolve_weight,
+    )
+
+    path = materialize_weight(resolve_weight(path))
+    if path.endswith(".safetensors"):
+        from safetensors.torch import load_file
+
+        state = load_file(path, device="cpu")
+    elif path.endswith((".pth", ".pt", ".bin")):
+        state = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
+    else:
+        raise ValueError("TinyVAE weights must be safetensors, pth, pt or bin")
+    model_name = TINY_VAE_ALIASES.get(model_name, model_name)
+    model_cls, channels = TINY_VAE_MODELS[model_name]
+    model = initialize_model(
+        model_cls, {"latent_channels": channels, "load_encoder": False}, dtype
+    )
+    if not isinstance(state, dict):
+        raise ValueError("TinyVAE checkpoint must contain a tensor state dictionary")
+    decoder_state = {}
+    expected = model.decoder.state_dict()
+    extras = []
+    for name, tensor in state.items():
+        if name.startswith(("encoder.", "taesd_encoder.")) or name in (
+            "vae_scale",
+            "vae_shift",
+        ):
+            continue
+        if name.startswith("taesd_decoder."):
+            name = name.removeprefix("taesd_decoder.")
+        elif name.startswith("decoder."):
+            name = name.removeprefix("decoder.")
+        if name not in expected:
+            extras.append(name)
+        else:
+            decoder_state[name] = tensor
+    if extras:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unexpected TinyVAE decoder weights: {extras}")
+    model.decoder.load_state_dict(decoder_state, strict=True)
+    return model.eval().requires_grad_(False)
+
+
+class TinyVAEDecodeWrapper(nn.Module):
+    """Keep the original VAE's raw-latent and pixel contracts at its boundary."""
+
+    # The temporal runner does not use the original decoder's spatial collectives.
+    use_parallel_decode = False
+
+    def __init__(self, original, tiny, model_name, pipeline_config):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.original = original
+        self.tiny = tiny
+        self.model_name = TINY_VAE_ALIASES.get(model_name, model_name)
+        self.pipeline_config = pipeline_config
+        if self.model_name in ("taeh3", "taew2_1", "taew2_2"):
+            arch = pipeline_config.vae_config.arch_config
+            device = next(tiny.parameters()).device
+            for name in ("latents_mean", "latents_std"):
+                value = torch.tensor(
+                    getattr(arch, name), device=device, dtype=torch.float32
+                ).view(1, -1, 1, 1, 1)
+                self.register_buffer(
+                    f"tiny_{name}",
+                    value,
+                    persistent=False,
+                )
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name):
+        try:
+            return super().__getattr__(name)
+        except AttributeError:
+            return getattr(super().__getattr__("original"), name)
+
+    def forward(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        return self.original(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    def _normalized_latents(self, latents):
+        if self.model_name == "taeltx2":
+            # LTX-2 receives raw latents from the AV decoding stage.
+            mean = self.original.latents_mean.to(latents).view(1, -1, 1, 1, 1)
+            std = self.original.latents_std.to(latents).view(1, -1, 1, 1, 1)
+            return (latents - mean) / std
+        if self.model_name in ("taeh3", "taew2_1", "taew2_2"):
+            mean = self.tiny_latents_mean.to(latents)
+            std = self.tiny_latents_std.to(latents)
+            return (latents - mean) / std
+        if self.model_name == "taef2" and latents.shape[1] == 32:
+            b, c, h, w = latents.shape
+            latents = latents.reshape(b, c, h // 2, 2, w // 2, 2)
+            latents = latents.permute(0, 1, 3, 5, 2, 4).reshape(b, 128, h // 2, w // 2)
+        scaling, shift = self.pipeline_config.get_decode_scale_and_shift(
+            latents.device, latents.dtype, self.original
+        )
+        if shift is not None:
+            latents = latents - shift
+        return latents if scaling is None else latents * scaling
+
+    def _pixels(self, latents):
+        normalized = self._normalized_latents(latents)
+        channels = normalized.shape[1]
+        if channels != self.tiny.latent_channels:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{self.model_name} expects {self.tiny.latent_channels} latent channels, got {channels}"
+            )
+        return self.tiny.decode(normalized.to(next(self.tiny.parameters()).dtype))
+
+    def decode(self, latents, return_dict=False, on_frames=None, **kwargs):
+        # Generic and LTX stages consume raw pixels in [-1, 1].
+        pixels = self._pixels(latents) * 2 - 1
+        if on_frames is not None:
+            on_frames(pixels)
+        return pixels
+
+    def decode_base(self, latents, on_frames=None, **kwargs):
+        # H3's processor owns ImageNet denormalization after decode_base.
+        pixels = self._pixels(latents)
+        mean = pixels.new_tensor((0.485, 0.456, 0.406)).view(1, 3, 1, 1, 1)

+        pixels = (pixels - mean) / std
+        if on_frames is not None:
+            on_frames(pixels)
+        return pixels
+
+    def prepare_decoder_autocast_weights(self, dtype):
+        return 0
+
+    def enable_tiling(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        # TinyVAE processes time sequentially. Original encoder tiling stays intact.
+        return self.original.enable_tiling(*args, **kwargs)
+

+"""TinyVAE latent contracts, temporal state isolation and checkpoint loading."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.vaes.tiny_autoencoder import (
+    TinyImageAutoencoder,
+    TinyVideoAutoencoder,
+)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("channels", [16, 24, 32, 48, 128])
+def test_video_batch_and_request_isolation(channels):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    model = TinyVideoAutoencoder(channels, load_encoder=False).eval()
+    z = torch.randn(2, channels, 2, 1, 1)
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        together = model.decode(z)
+        separately = torch.cat([model.decode(sample) for sample in z.split(1)])
+        torch.testing.assert_close(together, separately, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)
+        assert torch.equal(together, model.decode(z))
+    expected_frames = (
+        5 if channels == 24 else 2 * model.temporal_ratio - (model.temporal_ratio - 1)
+    )
+    assert together.shape == (
+        2,
+        3,
+        expected_frames,
+        8 * model.patch_size,
+        8 * model.patch_size,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("channels", [4, 16, 64, 128])
+def test_image_video_layout(channels):
+    model = TinyImageAutoencoder(channels, load_encoder=False).eval()
+    z = torch.randn(1, channels, 2, 1, 2)
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        frames = model.decode(z)
+        separately = torch.stack([model.decode(z[:, :, t]) for t in range(2)], dim=2)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(frames, separately)
+    assert frames.shape[1] == (4 if channels == 64 else 3)
+
+
+class Original(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(()))
+        self.register_buffer("latents_mean", torch.tensor([2.0]))
+        self.register_buffer("latents_std", torch.tensor([3.0]))
+
+    def encode(self, pixels):
+        return pixels + self.weight
+
+
+class Capture(nn.Module):
+    latent_channels = 1
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(()))
+
+    def decode(self, latents):
+        self.input = latents.clone()
+        return latents.expand(-1, 3, -1, -1, -1)
+
+
+def config(**arch):
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        vae_config=SimpleNamespace(arch_config=SimpleNamespace(**arch)),
+        get_decode_scale_and_shift=lambda device, dtype, vae: (0.5, 2.0),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "model_name", ["taesd", "taehv", "taeh3", "taew2_1", "taew2_2", "taeltx2"]
+)
+def test_wrapper_raw_latents_and_original_encoder(model_name):
+    original, tiny = Original(), Capture()
+    cfg = config(latents_mean=[2.0], latents_std=[3.0], video_decoder_variant="ltx_2")
+    wrapped = TinyVAEDecodeWrapper(original, tiny, model_name, cfg)
+    raw = torch.full((1, 1, 1, 1, 1), 5.0)
+    parts = []
+    pixels = wrapped.decode(raw, on_frames=parts.append)
+    expected = 1.0 if model_name in ("taeh3", "taew2_1", "taew2_2", "taeltx2") else 1.5
+    assert torch.equal(tiny.input, torch.full_like(raw, expected))
+    assert torch.equal(pixels, parts[0])
+    assert torch.equal(wrapped.encode(raw), original.encode(raw))
+    assert not wrapped.use_parallel_decode
+    wrapped.to(torch.float64)
+    assert wrapped.tiny.weight.dtype == wrapped.original.weight.dtype == torch.float64
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("variant", ["ltx_2_3", "ltx_2_5"])

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["flux", "wan21", "wan22", "qwen21", "ltx2"])
+def test_pipeline_normalization_roundtrip(kind):
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.pipeline_configs.flux import FluxPipelineConfig
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.pipeline_configs.ltx_2 import LTX2PipelineConfig
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.pipeline_configs.qwen_image21 import (
+        QwenImage21PipelineConfig,
+    )
+    from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.pipeline_configs.wan import (
+        Wan2_2_TI2V_5B_Config,
+        WanT2V480PConfig,
+    )
+
+    cases = {
+        "flux": (FluxPipelineConfig, "taef1", 16),
+        "wan21": (WanT2V480PConfig, "taew2_1", 16),
+        "wan22": (Wan2_2_TI2V_5B_Config, "taew2_2", 48),
+        "qwen21": (QwenImage21PipelineConfig, "taeqi2_1", 64),
+        "ltx2": (LTX2PipelineConfig, "taeltx2", 128),
+    }
+    cls, name, channels = cases[kind]
+    cfg = cls()
+    # Mirror VAELoader: pipeline defaults are placeholders until config.json
+    # updates the VAE architecture and derived normalization tensors.
+    if kind == "flux":
+        cfg.vae_config.update_model_arch(
+            {"scaling_factor": 0.3611, "shift_factor": 0.1159}
+        )
+    elif kind == "wan22":
+        cfg.vae_config.update_model_arch(
+            {
+                "z_dim": 48,
+                "latents_mean": tuple(torch.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 48).tolist()),
+                "latents_std": tuple(torch.linspace(0.5, 1.5, 48).tolist()),
+            }
+        )
+    original = Original()
+    if kind == "ltx2":
+        original.latents_mean = torch.randn(channels)
+        original.latents_std = torch.rand(channels) + 0.5
+    normalized = torch.randn(1, channels, 2, 2, 2)
+    scale, shift = cfg.get_decode_scale_and_shift(
+        normalized.device, normalized.dtype, original
+    )
+    raw = normalized / scale
+    if shift is not None:
+        raw = raw + shift
+    wrapped = TinyVAEDecodeWrapper(original, Capture(), name, cfg)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(wrapped._normalized_latents(raw), normalized)
+
